raw_response:
I've been working this land in Quzhou for 30 years. I know this ground. The wheat-maize rotation is my backbone — reliable, familiar, and the grain prices have been steady enough. Cotton I still grow on a smaller piece, but at 58 and farming alone, I'm honest with myself: I can't manage too much cotton anymore. Harvest wears me down and hiring hands costs money I'd rather keep.

I'll put 30 mu into wheat-maize rotation — winter wheat goes in October, summer maize follows right after harvest in June. That leaves 10 mu for cotton. I've thought about dropping cotton entirely, but I know how to grow it, and it gives me some income diversity. 10 mu I can manage.

For wheat, I'll use improved seed — Kenong 199 or similar, whatever the village supply station has. I've used it for years. I'll apply fertilizer at base and top-dress at jointing. Irrigation three times: pre-winter watering, jointing stage, and heading. That's what the land needs here.

For maize after wheat, I go no-till — straight seeding into the stubble saves me time and my back. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 type. Maize gets summer rains mostly, but I'll irrigate twice to be safe with the well.

Cotton gets ploughed land, more potassium than the grain crops, more pesticide too — aphids and bollworm are always trouble. Six spray rounds is what experience tells me. I'll do the topping myself.
